Hi Jules / Patrick,

Great to hear—thanks for the spreadsheet. Short answers up top: our connector supports both modes: (A) Ingest raw artifacts into a EU-only S3 bucket with automated redaction hooks, and (B) accept pre-redacted artifacts for immediate storage when customers require it.

Redaction matrix (high level):
- PII (names, emails): configurable removal or tokenization
- IP addresses: default partial redaction (last octet masked), configurable full-IP masking
- Auth tokens/credentials: full removal from logs by default
- Stack traces: we can redact file paths/line numbers; we preserve hashed identifiers for traceability

Operational points:
- We produce an immutable audit record (sha256) for each artifact and metadata showing which redaction rules were applied.
- Unredaction: supported for short windows (admin-only) when legal/incident teams require a court/forensics process; we log every unredaction event and restrict it to named roles.

I've attached the connector spec and a short MAP (mutual action plan) template so we can align on milestones. A few quick asks from our side:
1) Confirm EU data residency requirement in writing (so we can lock region to eu-west-1 for Acme).
2) Any regulatory constraints beyond SOC2 (e.g., local privacy regs) that should change redaction defaults?

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical sync Wed (Dec 2) or Thu (Dec 3). Sergio and I will join.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Kim / Priyom—forwarding Patrick's questions. Short recommended approach from infra/security:

1) Deterministic hashing: we prefer customer-supplied deterministic salted hashes (customer manages salt). If customer cannot salt deterministically, we can accept raw and apply a per-customer server-side salt and store the salt in an encrypted KMS-backed secret. That meets the correlation requirement but adds a key-management step in the SOW.

2) PCAPs: recommend a two-step flow: pre-ingest client-side redaction for payloads (PII removal) + upload of header-only PCAPs for obvious traffic correlation. For forensic needs we offer an "escrow" flow: encrypted transfer of raw PCAP to a short-lived holding bucket accessible only under documented legal request process.

Action items for Priyom: please draft the SOW language that covers (a) EU-only bucket enforcement, (b) deterministic-hash options, and (c) the PCAP escrow process with an audit trail. Add a clause about unredaction approval matrix.

Sergio
Senior Security Architect, Redwood Inference
